title: Tooling: batch exact rows for the quadratic-affine rank witness (8.4x faster check, no new kappa)
body:
**Tooling improvement; no new kappa.** Verification engineering (track 85-94, seed 89). Base commit `2921874911956718fcaaaf9396fe8267b3cfa9f0`. Prepared with help from opencode.

## What changes

`scripts/audit_quadratic_affine.py` (part of `make verify-certificates`) builds twelve exact quadratic-affine rank witnesses; its hot path `rank_witness` in `scripts/experiments/quadratic_affine.py` constructed each row with one `inner` call per (row, column) pair (160,135,378 calls in the heavy fixture). This replaces that loop with an exact bit-sliced batched engine (lane-packed character masks, even-lane SWAR zero test, collision-free staged stride-8 gather). `inner`, the fixtures and all mathematical outputs are unchanged.

Measured on the same host and input (CPython 3.13.15, Windows):

| Run | Wall time |
|---|---:|
| `scripts/audit_quadratic_affine.py` at base | 89.1 s |
| `scripts/audit_quadratic_affine.py` with this change | 10.6 s (8.4x) |
| Row construction, all fixtures, reference vs batched | 67.0 s -> 3.56 s |

The regenerated `certificates/quadratic-affine-vectors.json` differs from the base commit in **exactly one line**: the recorded hash of the edited source file. Every case record, row digest, binary rank and span control is byte-identical.

## Verification

`sh
python3 -B research/quadratic-affine-performance/benchmark.py --out /tmp/qa-benchmark.json
`

Expected final line: `PASS identical rows (14662 rows, 0 mismatches); certificate equals committed; controls: odd-lane false positive demonstrated, dropped gather stage detected`.

All 14,662 witness rows (including all 12,623 rows of the heavy fixture) are compared against the verbatim base-commit reference engine; the full certificate is recomputed and required to equal the committed file, and the committed base-commit snapshot `evidence/base-certificate.json` must differ only in the edited source's hash. `research/quadratic-affine-performance/test_engine.py` (11 tests) adds brute-force primitive comparisons with borrow-chain adversaries, randomized family samples, unchanged rejection paths, and negative controls (odd-lane SWAR false positive; dropped gather stage; one-bit row corruption changing the digest). The suite was red-green verified: a deliberately dropped gather stage fails 5 tests. `tests/test_quadratic_affine.py` passes unchanged and `python3 -B scripts/verify_selected_result.py` still reports the selected kappa.

## Overlap

[PR 752](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/752) (Curtis Dransfield, seed 92) reached this hotspot first with a non-invasive packed-lane adapter (73.4 s -> 10.96 s on macOS arm64). Credit to them. This PR is an independent second implementation that additionally (1) wires the speedup into the shipped check so the default `make verify-certificates` run gets faster, (2) machine-checks the one-line certificate diff against a committed base-commit snapshot, and (3) corroborates the packed-lane conclusion from a different lane design with red-green verified negative controls.

## Scope

No certificate content, bound, kappa value, patch, generator, proof supplement, pinned source or `upstream/` file changes; only `scripts/experiments/quadratic_affine.py`, its regenerated certificate (one line), and the evidence package `research/quadratic-affine-performance/`. This is a finite-check speedup, not a formal proof of any theorem. The unchanged GF(2) elimination is now the runtime floor. Full `make verify`, the selected cold replay, Lean and remote Linux CI were not run; only the affected checks above were. Apache-2.0.
